chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who misses the Maghrib prayer until the time of 'Atamah ('Isha) arrives. He said: “If the time of 'Atamah has arrived and he remembers that he owes the Maghrib prayer, then if he wishes he may begin with Maghrib, and if he wishes he may begin with 'Atamah, then pray Maghrib afterward.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is anomalous, and the established basis is what we have mentioned previously: that when the time is ample, one should begin with the missed prayer, and if the time is constrained, he begins with the current prayer. There is no time here in which a person is given a choice. As for what he narrated:

key_terms.الْوَقْتُ مُضَيَّقًا: a constrained time window requiring priority to the current prayer
key_terms.الْوَقْتُ وَاسِعًا: a time window broad enough to perform prayers in order
key_terms.شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report not relied upon as the primary ruling

ai.seo_question: If someone misses Maghrib until 'Isha time begins, which prayer should be performed first?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the order of performing missed Maghrib prayer and the present 'Isha prayer when both are due. The transmitted report gives a choice, but Muhammad ibn al-Hasan rejects it as anomalous and affirms the juristic principle that the missed prayer takes precedence when time is ample, while the current prayer takes precedence when time is tight.
